name: Heather grey
lede: Heather grey is a dusty, purplish grey standardized by RAL in 1927, named after the small flowering shrub whose dried blooms turn this same muted purple-grey rather than the bright pink of its fresh flowers.

sections.title: A dried flower's grey
sections.body:
RAL 1927 is the source given for Heather grey here, with the hex value an approximate screen rendering of the printed standard [1]. The plant heather flowers in a vivid magenta-pink, but its clipped and dried sprigs, long sold for mourning wreaths and wall decoration, fade toward the grey-purple this name captures; the color library groups it under "heather" as a family word alongside brighter heather shades [2]. In Munsell terms it sits near 9.8PB 4.4/3.2: a dark, low-chroma violet-grey [2].

The nearest named colors are [[plumbago-slate|Plumbago Slate]], 5.4 units away and duller, and [[deep-slate-violet|Deep Slate-Violet]], 5.5 units away, purpler and darker [2]. The library also lists Greyish Campanula Purple and Pearl Blackberry as alternate names landing in the same spot [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Heather grey appears in 77 of our 23,781 paintings, as photographed, rarer than 53 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 12 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.9 times the expected rate, and is most over-represented in French paintings, at 2.3 times expected [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color [3]. The earliest match, in a work by Filippo Lippi, is dated 1460, 467 years before RAL's 1927 standard — a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof that any heather-based dye was used, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

origin.named_after: heather, the flowering shrub, in its dried and faded state

questions.q: Why does Heather grey look grey rather than the plant's bright pink?
choices: It is named for heather's dried, faded sprigs
It is an unrelated word that only sounds like heather
It is named for a grey heath landscape, not the flower
questions.answer: It is named for heather's dried, faded sprigs

questions.q: True or false: Heather grey most often appears as the brightest area of a painting.

openers: Heather grey is a flower color, but it's the dried flower's color, not the fresh one.
